metadata.title: CoreWeave’s Banks to Sell $4.5 Billion Meta-Tied Loan Next Week

content.text:
(Bloomberg) -- CoreWeave Inc.'s bankers at Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc. are preparing a $4.5 billion loan sale for as soon as next week, with the financing secured by graphics processing units for Meta Platforms Inc.

CoreWeave can draw on the proceeds of this debt sale from an escrow account that will fund GPUs for a data center in Dalton, Georgia, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The debt is expected to be paid down gradually over the life of the loan, the people said, asking not to be identified as the details are private.
The debt sale from the junk-rated neocloud was already expected to carry investment-grade ratings, thanks to its contract with Meta. But it's coming at a challenging time, with CoreWeave one of the companies at the heart of investor concerns about the potential payoff from the massive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Adding to the worries, billions of dollars in loans tied to Chinese firms are now on pause, as new US curbs on chip access threatens Asia's burgeoning AI debt financing market.
CoreWeave helped soothe nerves briefly earlier this month when its full-year revenue exceeded both its previous forecast and Wall Street's average estimate, but on Wednesday, the cost to protect the company's debt against default for five years increased by the most ever. The swaps are pricing in a more than 70% chance of default within the next half-decade.
CoreWeave's 9% bond due in 2031 was trading at record lows to yield 18% on Wednesday, according to Trace. That's paying more than double what the loan transaction could yield, with initial discussions focusing around 7% to 7.5%, the people with knowledge said. Still, potential investors have already registered indications of interest in line with the transaction size, one of the people said. The company's delayed draw term loans are trading around par, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.
Details and timing of the deal are still being finalized and could change, the people said.
Representatives for CoreWeave and Morgan Stanley declined to comment, while spokespeople for MUFG and Meta didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.
